statutes.act: Or Any Other Provision Of The Code

facts: On 13.6.1979, the VII Addl. Sessions Judge, Bulandshahar, recorded an order convicting the appellants under Sections 366 and 368 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years with a fine of Rs.100/- each.
The appellants filed an appeal against this order in the High Court of Allahabad.
On 18.6.1979, the appeal was admitted by the High Court and notice was issued.
The High Court also issued an interim stay on the execution of the sentence and the realization of fine while granting bail to the appellants.
On 28.11.1990, the matter came up for hearing before the High Court.
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in dismissing the appeal filed by the accused-appellants against the order of conviction and sentence issued by the trial court, for non-prosecution.
What is the procedure to be followed by the Appellate Court when hearing an appeal not dismissed summarily?
Can the Appellate Court dispose of the appeal after perusing the record on its own or must it adjourn the appeal to a future date and intimate the accused to be present on the next date of hearing?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants argued that the High Court was not justified in dismissing their appeal for non-prosecution.
They contended that the Appellate Court must peruse the record before disposing of the appeal.
respondent_arguments: The respondent/State argued that the High Court was justified in dismissing the appeal for non-prosecution.
They contended that the Appellate Court can dispose of the appeal after perusing the record on its own, without hearing the parties.
court_reasoning: The court held that once the Appellate Court admits an appeal and issues notice to the parties, it must send for the record and hear the parties before finally deciding the appeal.
It ruled that the requirement to send for the record is not an idle formality but casts an obligation on the court to decide the appeal only after it has perused the record.
The court held that the Appellate Court can dispose of the appeal after perusing the record, even if the parties are absent.
holding: The Supreme Court set aside the order of the High Court and remanded the matter to it for 'passing an appropriate order in accordance with law after hearing the appellants or their counsel and on their failure to engage counsel, after hearing counsel appointed by the Court to argue on their behalf'.
